key_insight: CompMat-Bench benchmarks AI agents on realistic computational materials research steps by precomputing expensive simulation inputs/outputs, enabling fixed-rule evaluation without rerunning costly experiments.
engineering_relevance: The benchmark helps materials scientists and tool builders compare agent performance on practical research workflows and identify where agents fail before deploying them in expensive simulation pipelines.
method: Built 94 tasks from recently published computational materials studies
Reproduced simulation inputs and outputs in advance as ground truth
Evaluated agents under four settings: single tasks vs. workflows, each with full vs. reduced guidance
evidence_signal: Across 94 tasks, agents based on three LLMs reached 66.0%–90.4% pass rates on single tasks with full guidance, while longer workflows and reduced guidance degraded performance.
watch_item: Results may depend on how closely benchmark tasks and fixed grading rules match real laboratory or simulation workflows, so transfer to new materials problems should be validated carefully.
paper_title: CompMat-Bench: Benchmarking AI Agents for Computational Materials Science
